1.13 Native byte workers

The Python archive layer can select a native worker with DNG_BYTE_BACKEND:

DNG_BYTE_BACKEND="$PWD/rust-scanner/target/release/byte-verify" \
uv run python preserve_apo.py scan /media/source/foto /media/reference/foto \
  archives/source --delta --workers 2 --rate-mib 64

Use $PWD/byte-verify-oxcaml to select the OCaml worker on macOS. Both support:

hash FILE
compare SOURCE REFERENCE
delta REFERENCE SOURCE DELTA EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA256

compare prints source SHA-256, reference SHA-256 and equality 1 or 0, tab separated. An empty reference argument requests source hashing without a reference. delta outputs its own SHA only after reconstruction passes. Workers own bounded buffers and the external xdelta process; Python owns file identity, inventory, checkpoint and acceptance. Direct worker calls do not supply those wider guards. Native byte operations are whole-file operations, not stored-sample or Lightroom-native fingerprint calculations.
